title: reservoirized-canary-autoscaler-and-burst-hedge-instrumentation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a reservoir-backed canary autoscaler and new burst-hedge telemetry. Improves canary stability during transient spikes and adds utilization delta reporting for dedicated fleets.
body:
Background and motivation: We've observed oscillations during canary rollouts when small transient spikes exhaust short-term burst capacity and trigger emergency throttles, which in turn abort canaries prematurely. This PR introduces a reservoirized canary autoscaler that maintains a soft reservoir of reserved headroom for canary traffic and a burst-hedge instrumentation layer that surfaces delta-based utilization signals to the operator console. The goal is to reduce false-negative canary failures and keep throughput guarantees intact for committed tenants.

What this PR does (high level): 1) New controller: reservoir_canary_controller that allocates a transient reservoir for canaries; it decays over a configurable window and replenishes from unused reserved capacity. 2) Burst-hedge telemetry: instrumentation that emits reservoir_headroom, burst_consumption_rate, and canary_saturation_index. 3) Utilization delta reporter: per-fleet periodic summary that computes 1m/5m/1h deltas and percentiles to feed the capacity advisor. 4) Config + feature flag: featureFlag.reservoir_canary_v2 gated rollout and a canaryPolicy config block for tuning. 5) Tests: unit, integration, and a focused e2e that simulates microbursts during canary ramps.

Why this approach: Traditional autoscalers either aggressively provision (costly) or react slowly (latency regressions). A small, reservoir-backed canary path smooths transient demand while preserving global throughput SLAs by borrowing against a decaying short-term allowance instead of permanently reallocating capacity. The instrumentation provides visibility needed to debug and calibrate policies.

Design notes and constraints: - Reservoir semantics: time-decayed credit pool (default half-life 5m) scoped to the canary job; credits are drained on token issuance and replenished from idle reserved slots. - Safety fences: if fleet utilization > 92% for 1m sustained, reservoir borrowing is disabled and the canary is paused to preserve contractual throughput. - Accounting: we emit chargeback metrics so billing reports reflect borrowed consumption. - Backward compatibility: defaults off; existing autoscaler behaviors unchanged until feature flag enabled.

Config example (defaults):
reservoirPolicy:
  enabled: true
  max_credits: 50
  half_life_seconds: 300
  disable_threshold_pct: 92

Implementation summary (commits): - Add controller scaffolding and reconciliation loop with reservoir state machine. - Wire telemetry to internal/telemetry with new metric names and labels (fleet_id, tenant_id, canary_id). - Add utilization delta sampler that publishes to /metrics and to the capacity-advisor event bus. - Chart changes to expose feature flag and tune default reservoir size for Dedicated clusters. - Extensive tests: unit mocks for clock, integration with warm pool simulator, e2e microburst harness.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests cover state transitions, decay math, and limits. - Integration harness validates interactions with warm pool allocator. - E2E verified on staging dedicated cluster (dedicated-staging-3) with 1000 simulated tenants and scheduled microbursts. - Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag for internal canaries in staging for 1 week, gradual opt-in for canary runs in selected customers, full opt-in via console toggle after telemetry confirms stability (target 2 weeks).

Backwards compat and migrations: No DB schema changes. Metrics additions are additive. Operators can disable via feature flag or cluster-level config.

Related tickets and docs: Linear ENG-4821 (canary stability), ENG-4950 (utilization telemetry), SUP-1342 (support case: canary flapping). A short doc will be added to docs/dedicated/canary.md in a follow-up describing tuning knobs and troubleshooting.

Open questions and follow-ups: - Default reservoir sizing heuristics: current defaults are conservative; we plan an automatic-suggest feature in Optimize. - Long-term billing model: how to reflect transient borrowed credits in reserved billing.

Merge notes: Squash merge after approvals. Feature gated and behind a runtime flag for safe rollout.

review_comments: Ava Patel: Can we add a unit test that verifies reservoir disables when fleet utilization crosses the safety threshold?
Maya Chen: Added test and a small refactor to permit injecting a mocked fleetutil check (see test/e2e).
Jonas Klein: Concerned about metric cardinality — canary_id at high cardinality could blow up TSDB. Suggest sample_rate or label reduction.
Maya Chen: Reduced canary_id to 'canary_group' label and added sampling on low-cardinality clusters; documented tradeoffs in telemetry/README.
